scope: Focused narrative primary-source audit, not a systematic review or meta-analysis; no claim of exhaustive coverage through verification date.

original_paper.title: Invasive spinal cord computer interfaces for medicine and human capability: A mechanistic review and hypothesis paper on motor learning and sustained physiological control
original_paper.status: Read-only starting hypothesis paper; no original biological experiments; illustrative curves are not measurements.

references.title: Surface circumferential spinal cord recording in freely moving rodents
references.author_string: El Hadwe S, Ruiz-Mateos Serrano R, Psaltakis G, Forner M, Lee C, Swedick S, Banta A, Zhang X, Ghannam M, Hasan T, Carnicer-Lombarte A, Malliaras GG, Barone DG.
references.cohort: 15 rats overall; motor-decoding subset 5; 3 acute pigs.
references.access_and_signal: Intradural circumferential surface recording; external movement/stimulus labels.
references.supported_claim: Short-term recordings contained movement- and stimulus-related information; motor decoding used pooled bidirectional recurrent analysis.
references.not_established: Not a prospective chronic human decoder, expert-skill code, or demonstration of retained transfer.
references.scci_rh_inference: Useful causal features and chronic stability remain explicit SCCI_RH premises.
references.verification_depth: Full publisher text and author XML; Results Figs.1, 4, 5 and Methods.
references.source_quality_note: Figure 5 describes 21.29% as uniform chance across 8 classes; uniform chance is 12.5%. Its largest listed class is 215/1010=21.29%. Seek clarification; do not adopt that baseline.

references.title: A Hyperflexible Electrode Array for Long-Term Recording and Decoding of Intraspinal Neuronal Activity
references.author_string: Fan J, Li X, Wang P, Yang F, Zhao B, Yang J, Zhao Z, Li X.
references.cohort: 5 mice for nine-week recording; separate movement-decoding experiment in 2 mice.
references.access_and_signal: Penetrating ventral-horn electrodes; L1-L2 recording cohort and L3 decoding experiment.
references.supported_claim: Hyperflexible arrays enabled longitudinal intraspinal acquisition and wheel-running movement reconstruction.
references.not_established: Does not validate nonpenetrating human electrodes, indefinite stable channels, or fine expert finger information.
references.scci_rh_inference: Recording access and durability cannot be transferred across electrode types without an assumption.
references.verification_depth: Full publisher text and author XML; sections 2.2, 2.4.

references.title: Flexible circumferential bioelectronics to enable 360-degree recording and stimulation of the spinal cord
references.author_string: Woodington BJ, Lei J, Carnicer-Lombarte A, Güemes-González A, Naegele TE, Hilton S, El-Hadwe S, Trivedi RA, Malliaras GG, Barone DG.
references.cohort: 16 acute rats; separate 6 passive dummy implants; human cadaver feasibility.
references.access_and_signal: Circumferential rat epidural recording/stimulation; cadaver method includes durotomy and intradural passage.
references.supported_claim: Recorded spinal events triggered stimulation across acute complete transection; experimental cortical stimulation generated test input.
references.not_established: Passive six-week implants were not chronic active interfaces; cadaver placement was not functional human testing.
references.scci_rh_inference: Provides a spinal-recording-to-stimulation precedent; voluntary chronic control remains a further premise.
references.verification_depth: Author full-text XML; Figs.5-7 and acute/cadaver Methods.

references.title: A computational model for epidural electrical stimulation of spinal sensorimotor circuits
references.author_string: Capogrosso M, Wenger N, Raspopovic S, Musienko P, Beauparlant J, Bassi Luciani L, Courtine G, Micera S.
references.journal: The Journal of neuroscience : the official journal of the Society for Neuroscience
references.cohort: Rat computational field/axon models and in-vivo experiments; total cohort not independently established here.
references.access_and_signal: Lumbosacral epidural electrical stimulation and motor/physiological observations.
references.supported_claim: In the studied setting, myelinated afferent recruitment engaged motor circuitry trans-synaptically.
references.not_established: Not universal direct motoneuron stimulation, arbitrary inhibition, or a contact-independent neural command.
references.scci_rh_inference: Specify a calibrated recruitment map and reachable directions.
references.verification_depth: Author abstract via Europe PMC PMID24305828; detailed parameter tables not re-audited.

references.title: Activity-dependent spinal cord neuromodulation rapidly restores trunk and leg motor functions after complete paralysis

references.author_string: Rowald A, Komi S, Demesmaeker R, Baaklini E, Hernandez-Charpak SD, Paoles E, Montanaro H, Cassara A, Becce F, Lloyd B, Newton T, Ravier J, Kinany N, D'Ercole M, Paley A, Hankov N, Varescon C, McCracken L, Vat M, Caban M, Watrin A, Jacquet C, Bole-Feysot L, Harte C, Lorach H, Galvez A, Tschopp M, Herrmann N, Wacker M, Geernaert L, Fodor I, Radevich V, Van Den Keybus K, Eberle G, Pralong E, Roulet M, Ledoux JB, Fornari E, Mandija S, Mattera L, Martuzzi R, Nazarian B, Benkler S, Callegari S, Greiner N, Fuhrer B, Froeling M, Buse N, Denison T, Buschman R, Wende C, Ganty D, Bakker J, Delattre V, Lambert H, Minassian K, van den Berg CAT, Kavounoudias A, Micera S, Van De Ville D, Barraud Q, Kurt E, Kuster N, Neufeld E, Capogrosso M, Asboth L, Wagner FB, Bloch J, Courtine G.

references.title: Spinal cord stimulation for upper limb motor function in people with chronic post-stroke hemiparesis: a feasibility trial
references.author_string: de Freitas RM, Bhatia S, Sorensen E, Verma N, Carranza E, Ensel S, Borda L, Boos A, Goldsmith J, Fisher LE, Fields DP, Powell MP, Gordon S, Balzer J, Friedlander RM, Wittenberg GF, Gerszten PC, Krakauer JW, Pirondini E, Weber DJ, Capogrosso M.
references.cohort: 7 post-stroke participants; 4-week implant period; finger improvement in 3 with residual connectivity.
references.access_and_signal: Two unilateral cervical epidural leads; external stimulator, EMG, movement and clinical assessments.
references.supported_claim: Immediate ON assistance and within-trial OFF changes were reported; maximum benefit required continued stimulation.
references.not_established: Not healthy novice acquisition, spinal-recording-based assistance, or proof that all ON benefit becomes retention.
references.scci_rh_inference: Score assistance, OFF retention and later follow-up separately.
references.verification_depth: Full publisher text and author XML; abstract, assessments and Discussion.

references.title: Targeted, activity-dependent spinal stimulation produces long-lasting motor recovery in chronic cervical spinal cord injury
references.author_string: McPherson JG, Miller RR, Perlmutter SI.
references.journal: Proceedings of the National Academy of Sciences of the United States of America
references.journal_abbreviation: Proc Natl Acad Sci U S A
references.cohort: 24 injured rats: 9 activity-dependent, 6 open-loop, 9 retraining-only; impairment-matched, not randomized.
references.access_and_signal: Forelimb EMG triggered intraspinal stimulation below cervical contusion.
references.supported_claim: Activity-linked treatment improved reaching recovery; benefit persisted 3 stimulation-free weeks with daily retraining.
references.not_established: Roughly doubled recovery endpoint is not a 2x healthy learning-speed multiplier or proof of the proposed STDP mechanism.
references.scci_rh_inference: Separate contingent practice, retained outcome, and the untested expert-information contribution.
references.verification_depth: Full primary PMC article; Results and Materials/Methods.

references.title: Spike-timing-dependent plasticity in primate corticospinal connections induced during free behavior
references.author_string: Nishimura Y, Perlmutter SI, Eaton RW, Fetz EE.
references.cohort: 2 monkeys; 19 conditioning sessions and 15 cell/site pairs are repeated observations.
references.access_and_signal: Cortical spikes triggered cervical intraspinal stimulation: hybrid brain-spine access.
references.supported_claim: Conditioning modified corticospinal connection strength; timing mattered and many effects eventually reverted.
references.not_established: Not spinal-only recording, expert imitation, or demonstrated healthy human whole-skill transfer.
references.scci_rh_inference: Retain absent, reversible and adverse adaptation regimes.
references.verification_depth: Author-hosted full manuscript and author abstract; Results and Experimental Procedures.

references.title: Operant conditioning of a spinal reflex can improve locomotion after spinal cord injury in humans
references.author_string: Thompson AK, Pomerantz FR, Wolpaw JR.
references.journal: The Journal of neuroscience : the official journal of the Society for Neuroscience
references.cohort: 13 people with SCI: 9 conditioning, 4 measurement controls; 6/9 conditioned successfully.
references.access_and_signal: Surface tibial-nerve stimulation and soleus EMG, rather than implanted spinal access.
references.supported_claim: Thirty-session H-reflex down-conditioning produced persistent reflex and locomotor changes in responders.
references.not_established: Not invasive SCCI or direct expert-to-learner neural transfer.
references.scci_rh_inference: Supports plasticity and individual-response variation without relabelling peripheral access.
references.verification_depth: Author-hosted full manuscript; Subjects, protocol and Results.

references.title: Electrical spinal cord stimulation must preserve proprioception to enable locomotion in humans with spinal cord injury
references.author_string: Formento E, Minassian K, Wagner F, Mignardot JB, Le Goff-Mignardot CG, Rowald A, Bloch J, Micera S, Capogrosso M, Courtine G.
references.cohort: 3 SCI participants plus computational/preclinical experiments; some sensory tasks had smaller subsets.
references.access_and_signal: Epidural stimulation, proprioceptive assessment, peripheral responses and locomotion.
references.supported_claim: Continuous stimulation could disrupt proprioceptive information; temporal/spatial strategies sought to preserve it.
references.not_established: Does not imply every waveform abolishes perception or determine a healthy-consumer penalty.
references.scci_rh_inference: Model sensory cost and assistance dependence; preserve a no-benefit case.
references.verification_depth: Author full-text XML; human sensory/locomotor Results and Methods.

references.title: Walking naturally after spinal cord injury using a brain-spine interface
references.author_string: Lorach H, Galvez A, Spagnolo V, Martel F, Karakas S, Intering N, Vat M, Faivre O, Harte C, Komi S, Ravier J, Collin T, Coquoz L, Sakr I, Baaklini E, Hernandez-Charpak SD, Dumont G, Buschman R, Buse N, Denison T, van Nes I, Asboth L, Watrin A, Struber L, Sauter-Starace F, Langar L, Auboiroux V, Carda S, Chabardes S, Aksenova T, Demesmaeker R, Charvet G, Bloch J, Courtine G.

references.access_and_signal: Implanted cortical recording controlled spinal epidural stimulation.

references.title: Neuroprosthetic baroreflex controls haemodynamics after spinal cord injury
references.author_string: Squair JW, Gautier M, Mahe L, Soriano JE, Rowald A, Bichat A, Cho N, Anderson MA, James ND, Gandar J, Incognito AV, Schiavone G, Sarafis ZK, Laskaratos A, Bartholdi K, Demesmaeker R, Komi S, Moerman C, Vaseghi B, Scott B, Rosentreter R, Kathe C, Ravier J, McCracken L, Kang X, Vachicouras N, Fallegger F, Jelescu I, Cheng Y, Li Q, Buschman R, Buse N, Denison T, Dukelow S, Charbonneau R, Rigby I, Boyd SK, Millar PJ, Moraud EM, Capogrosso M, Wagner FB, Barraud Q, Bezard E, Lacour SP, Bloch J, Courtine G, Phillips AA.
references.cohort: Multiple rodent experiments; 3 nonhuman primates; human proof of concept in 1 participant.
references.access_and_signal: Lower-thoracic targeted EES and measured pressure feedback; human MSNA is peripheral nerve recording.

references.title: Long-term safety and efficacy of closed-loop spinal cord stimulation to treat chronic back and leg pain (Evoke): a double-blind, randomised, controlled trial
references.author_string: Mekhail N, Levy RM, Deer TR, Kapural L, Li S, Amirdelfan K, Hunter CW, Rosen SM, Costandi SJ, Falowski SM, Burgher AH, Pope JE, Gilmore CA, Qureshi FA, Staats PS, Scowcroft J, Carlson J, Kim CK, Yang MI, Stauss T, Poree L, Evoke Study Group.
references.cohort: 134 randomized chronic-pain participants, 67/arm; 125 analyzed at 3 months and 118 at 12 months.
references.access_and_signal: Epidural evoked compound action potentials controlled stimulation amplitude.

references.title: A Pilot Feasibility Trial of Multi-Program Epidural Spinal Cord Stimulation for Bladder Function Recovery in Chronic Spinal Cord Injury
references.author_string: Hubscher CH, Wang S, Manning T, Angeli CA, Boakye M, Sharma P, Matelsky J, Christie B, Johnson E, Tenore F, Harkema SJ.
references.cohort: 4 consented; 3 implanted; 2 completed 12-month follow-up; 1 achieved high sustained voiding efficiency.
references.access_and_signal: Lumbosacral epidural programs, cystometry and external physiological assessment; user-switched home modes.
references.supported_claim: Personalized storage/voiding programs and training supported selected bladder-management outcomes.

references.title: Linear combinations of primitives in vertebrate motor control
references.author_string: Mussa-Ivaldi FA, Giszter SF, Bizzi E.
references.journal: Proceedings of the National Academy of Sciences of the United States of America
references.journal_abbreviation: Proc Natl Acad Sci U S A
references.cohort: Spinalized frogs; animal count not independently established from accessible abstract.
references.access_and_signal: Paired intraspinal stimulation sites and hindlimb endpoint-force measurement.
references.supported_claim: Combined activation approximately summed tested endpoint force fields.
references.not_established: Not a universal human primitive library, exact voluntary superposition, or a transferable electrode map.

references.title: Mind-Link
references.video_title_as_supplied: Making a Brain Computer Interface in My Garage
references.cohort: No functional implanted human BCI validation established by reviewed repository.
references.access_and_signal: Repository README/tree, firmware, PCB/Gerber, visualizer and print-file structure.
references.supported_claim: The public proof-of-concept repository gives an ambitious BCI concept inspectable engineering artifacts.
references.not_established: Repository presence is not validation of a functioning implanted biological interface.
references.scci_rh_inference: Credit the engineering progression while contributing original SCCI mechanisms and designs.
references.verification_depth: Official README/tree and commit reverified; fresh video/transcript retrieval throttled.
references.source_quality_note: The project introduction supplies the ideal-biological-interface account of the video; this audit does not claim a fresh complete viewing.
